title: Replacing the day 3 clinic visit with a nurse telephone review during spinal cord stimulator trials: a cost-consequence analysis
abstract: Objective: to compare health service and patient costs and the consequences of replacing the in-person day 3 visit during percutaneous spinal cord stimulator trials with a structured nurse telephone review. Design: cost-consequence analysis comparing all trial episodes in 2026 and 2027 in one regional pain service. Outcomes: health service cost per episode (primary), patient and companion costs, on-time implant decisions, unplanned attendances and infections. Results and conclusions will follow the 2027 data.
introduction: Trial-week visits cost patients long journeys and companions' working days, and retrieved studies suggest that a mid-trial visit rarely finds problems that patients do not report themselves. No published evaluation has costed the change from the patient perspective.
methods: All trial episodes started in 2026 and 2027 are included. Resource use comes from service, emergency department and theatre records, priced with local unit costs; patient costs are estimated from postcode distance in both years. The primary analysis is the difference in mean health service cost with a bootstrap interval; consequences are tabulated beside costs. The evaluation was classified as a service evaluation.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present case mix by year, the cost-consequence table for both perspectives, bootstrap intervals and the sensitivity analyses named in the protocol.
discussion: The discussion will weigh any saving against the consequences, compare the result with the retrieved before-after and randomised evidence, and state whether the pathway should extend to implant follow-up.
limitations: Historical comparison; patient costs estimated rather than measured before the change; one service; rare consequences imprecise.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not claim effects on pain outcomes or on the permanent implant rate.
summary: CHEERS-structured draft with results left empty until the 2027 data are analysed.
